rules.title: shopt / extglob is a bash builtin
rules.why: shopt is a bash builtin. PowerShell has no shell options table, so the command dies with "The term 'shopt' is not recognized". This is the exact failure reported in anthropics/claude-code#28670.
rules.pwsh: There is no equivalent and none is needed: PowerShell's own globbing plus Get-ChildItem -Include/-Exclude covers what extglob is normally used for. e.g. bash "rm !(keep.txt)" -> pwsh "Get-ChildItem -Exclude keep.txt | Remove-Item"

rules.title: extglob pattern !(...) / @(...) / +(...)
rules.why: Extended globs such as !(a|b) and @(a|b) are bash-only pattern syntax. PowerShell parses the parentheses as a sub-expression and either errors or silently matches nothing.
rules.pwsh: Use Get-ChildItem with -Include/-Exclude (both accept arrays), or a -match/-notmatch regex filter. e.g. "rm !(a|b)" -> "Get-ChildItem -Exclude a,b | Remove-Item"

rules.title: brace expansion {a,b}
rules.why: bash expands {a,b} into two words before running the command. PowerShell does not expand braces at all - it passes the literal text "{a,b}" through, so the command runs against a filename that does not exist.

rules.title: /dev/null does not exist on Windows
rules.why: /dev/null is a POSIX device file. On Windows PowerShell the redirection target is created as a literal file named "null" inside a "dev" directory, or the command fails because the path does not exist.
rules.pwsh: Redirect to $null:  "cmd > $null"  or, for all streams, "cmd *> $null"

rules.why: PowerShell does support "2>&1", but the bash idiom "> file 2>&1" is order-sensitive and the common "> /dev/null 2>&1" form silently creates a file. PowerShell's own redirect-everything operator is "*>".
rules.pwsh: Use "cmd *> $null" to discard everything, or "cmd *> out.log" to capture everything.
